sections.overview: Tunga penetrans is a flea that causes tungiasis in people and other animals.
sections.identification: The tiny adult female remains embedded in the skin, most often on the feet.
sections.habitat: Its immature stages develop in dry, shaded soil in tropical and subtropical settings.
sections.diet: Both sexes take blood meals; only fertilized females burrow into the host’s skin.
sections.behavior: After burrowing, the female remains partly exposed through a small skin opening while feeding and producing eggs.
sections.reproduction: The embedded female releases eggs into the environment, where larvae feed on organic debris before pupating.
sections.ecology: Tungiasis is a zoonosis affecting people and animals.
sections.conservation: WHO presents tungiasis as a zoonotic health problem.
